I held off on this one for a LONG time. Some of the negative reviews frightened me off, however, some of the mods, like Radious, gave me hope. Bought it the DLC on sale.

Refunded after only one hour. The game is just too difficult to be fun. I miss the old Rome Total War days. Even Shogun 2 is much for fun than this and easier to learn. There needs to be a balance between fun and difficulty and this one fails in that regard.

The other problem is I'm just not interested in ancient Chinese history. I knew this going in, but thought I would give it a try anyway.

Despite my feelings, I'm giving this a thumbs up because I respect game developers and the hard work involved. Some have found this game extremely fun and rewarding. I wish I was one of them.

This game is not worth it, there are many other games from the total war franchise that are better than this, but the diplomacy in this game is probably the best in the franchise. If you want to buy this just for the story (China's three kingdom era) then go ahead and try it out.

Bugs and broken mechanics for a game that looked promising but never got the attention it deserved from the developers. Broken DLC added to the problems. Creative Assembly abandoned the game after promising much delivering little.
I found it overly complicated and not as intuitively understable as the Rome installment of the series. It never really drew me. The systems put me off playing the game.

Pros
- Some great new mechanics with the diplomacy. However, I don't like the barter system in these newer titles, but in some instances it's historically accurate so eh.
- working your way up to being an emperor is pretty cool.
Cons
- Everyone pretty much has the same roster,
- Don't feel like playing it again after the one campaign. Rome 2, Attila, Shogun 2, Med 2, Nptw, and Empire all had great replayability for me
- Not a fan of the UI, immersion doesn't feel quite the same anymore. I dont feel like any of these modern "historical" titles are truly historical anymore (too arcadey for me).

All in all some new good mechanics I feel should stay in franchise, but still wish I saved my money for something else

Keeps crashing at unpredictable timings (during map phase, in battle or transiting to a battle) with no clear fix which makes me frustrated and try to quick save at every occasion.

One of my biggest frustrations was how the game ends once the Yellow Turbans control a certain percentage of the map. I had invested a lot of hours into building a strong kingdom and was confident I could eventually defeat them—so having the campaign suddenly end felt unfair and anticlimactic.

The battle scenes also felt somewhat comical and lacked the intensity I was hoping for. Overall, there isn’t much real action; most of the gameplay seems to be spent moving units around the map rather than engaging in meaningful combat.

That said, the diplomacy system is genuinely impressive and was one of the few aspects I really enjoyed. The leader rank system, which unlocks additional options, is also a good idea, but it isn’t very intuitive and takes too long to understand.

In the end, it’s a decent game, but compared to other entries in the series, it doesn’t live up to the standard I associate with Total War.

It's a deeply flawed game, the systems are very noisy and most of the time you feel like you're just doing pointless busywork and are systemically discouraged from actually playing the game. However, when the circumstances are just right and the game throws you into a dramatic, challenging situations, Three Kingdoms shines very brightly. Excellent visual style, very well illustrated and memorable characters.
The main area I'd look at improving is the experiential relationship with the Delegate/Autoresolve function, and the tipping point around turn 100 where you cannot be stopped, but still need to play for another 100 turns to paint the map. More dramatic and emergent storytelling please, fewer pointless accounting number-games.

It's a great Total War game. It has the best diplomacy in the whole series. However, the UI can be overwhelming with the amount of data it gives to you at one time. The actual battles are solid but a little stale considering the lack of unit diversity. Lack of replayability is also an issue, since it's hard to tell the differences from faction to faction. It's worth your time if your a long-time fan of the series, but I sincerely doubt this will be your favorite entry.

Three Kingdoms is easily the best game in Creative Assembly's Total War series, at least among those I've played. The diplomacy, settlement management, and unit types have been made more complex without becoming needlessly dense, and the battles feel better than ever. However, the best and most unique innovation within Three Kingdoms can be found in Romance mode, which makes your generals as strong as their mythical representations in the Chinese historical canon.

honestly... just not a fun game. tedious and unrewarding even when you do win. The combat is underwhelming. Despite the AI being toted as the best in the series, it really isn't that great... unless countries making random ridiculous demands and going to war over it with you is somehow good AI? You also quite literally cannot make any trade or diplomacy that isn't massively to your disadvantage, so there isn't any point in using diplomacy. it is constant min-maxing for no real aim or satisfaction.

The game is great but support for it was cut short. Historically important points of time such as the Battle of Red Cliffs and the actual Three Kingdoms period are missing entirely, and will never be there. It's still a great game, but beware what you're getting into in terms of support.

Also, I recently tried to load a save of mine, and I couldn't do it because the game claimed the save uses DLC that was not installed. This is simply not true, as I had all the DLC I own installed and enabled. Starting a new game wouldn't work either! Going offline in Steam seemed to solve the issue, so I can only assume the issue is caused by some sort of a poor DRM thing.

This is without a doubt one of the best "historical" Total War game. Even though I played most Total War, I felt a bit lost at first because of the surprising amount of new or changed stuff in this game which is refreshing. There are a lot of things that are done better than in previous games like the diplomacy system and even the AI behaviour in battle changing with the difficulty instead of just stats differences.

The only "issue" I have with this game (and probably with most future historical games) is the existence of Total War: Warhammer that almost nullify the repetitiveness I quickly felt in Three Kingdoms after playing more than a campaign.
